facts.statement: The genus Cricosaurus was established by Johann Andreas Wagner in 1858 based on three skulls found in the Late Jurassic of Germany.
facts.quote: The genus was established by Johann Andreas Wagner in 1858 for three skulls from the Tithonian (Late Jurassic) of Germany.

facts.statement: Wagner originally described a specimen in 1852 as 'Stenosaurus elegans' before reclassifying it as Cricosaurus in 1858 based on fossils from a quarry in Daiting, Bavaria.
facts.quote: Cricosaurus was first named by Wagner in 1858 based on three specimens from a quarry in Daiting, (Bavaria, Germany), as a reclassification of a specimen he had previously described in 1852

facts.statement: Cricosaurus was an extinct marine crocodyliform that lived during the Late Jurassic period.
facts.quote: Cricosaurus is an extinct genus of marine crocodyliforms of the Late Jurassic.

facts.statement: Fossils of Cricosaurus have been found in Late Jurassic deposits across England, France, Switzerland, Germany, Argentina, Cuba, and Mexico, as well as in the earliest Cretaceous of Argentina.
facts.quote: Fossil specimens referrable to Cricosaurus are known from Late Jurassic deposits in England, France, Switzerland, Germany, Argentina (Vaca Muerta), Cuba (Jagua Formation), and Mexico (La Caja and Pimienta Formations). and from the earliest Cretaceous (lower Berriasian) of Argentina.

facts.statement: Cricosaurus was a relatively small reptile, with species like C. suevicus reaching 2 meters and C. araucanensis reaching 3.2 meters in total body length.
facts.quote: It was a relatively small reptile, with C. suevicus and C. araucanensis measuring 2 m and 3.2 m in total body length, respectively.

facts.statement: Both juveniles and adults of C. araucanensis possessed well-developed salt glands, allowing them to drink salt water and eat prey with high ionic concentration without dehydrating.
facts.quote: Recent examination of the fossil specimens of Cricosaurus araucanensis have shown that both juveniles and adults of this species had well-developed salt glands.

facts.statement: The long-snouted species C. suevicus likely fed mostly on fish.
facts.quote: The long-snouted C. suevicus and R. gracilis would have fed mostly on fish

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that viviparity (live birth) was more likely than oviparity for Cricosaurus based on an evaluation of reproductive hypotheses.
facts.quote: In an evaluation of different reproductive hypotheses for Cricosaurus and other metriorhynchids, Herrera et al. considered viviparity more likely than oviparity.

facts.statement: A comprehensive 2009 analysis confirmed the validity of Cricosaurus species and reclassified several long-snouted species from related genera like Geosaurus and Metriorhynchus into Cricosaurus.
facts.quote: However, a more comprehensive analysis in 2009 showed that the species contained in Cricosaurus were valid, and furthermore that several long-snouted species formerly classified in the related genera Geosaurus, Enaliosuchus and Metriorhynchus were in fact more closely related to the original specimens of Cricosaurus, and thus were re-classified into this genus.

facts.quote: subordo: Thalattosuchia

facts.statement: It is debated whether Cricosaurus forms a monophyletic group, as some phylogenetic analyses have not supported its monophyly.
facts.quote: Some phylogenetic analysis did not support the monophyly of Cricosaurus

facts.statement: The genus Cricosaurus was originally named by Wagner in 1858 as a reclassification of a specimen he had previously described in 1852.
facts.quote: Cricosaurus fue nombrado originalmente por Wagner en 1858 como una reclasificación de un espécimen que él previamente había descrito en 1852.

facts.statement: An extensive analysis conducted in 2009 showed that the species contained within Cricosaurus were valid.
facts.quote: un análisis más extenso realizado en 2009 mostró que las especies contenidas en Cricosaurus eran válidas

facts.statement: All currently known species of Cricosaurus were three meters or less in length.
facts.quote: Todas las especies actualmente conocidas tenían unos tres metros o menos de largo.

facts.statement: Cricosaurus had a streamlined body and a finned tail, making it a more efficient swimmer than modern crocodiles.
facts.quote: Su cuerpo era ahusado para mayor eficiencia hidrodinámica, lo que junto a su cola con aleta lo hacían un nadador más eficiente que los cocodrilos modernos.

facts.statement: Recent examination of Cricosaurus araucanensis fossils showed that both juveniles and adults developed salt glands.
facts.quote: Un examen reciente de los fósiles de Cricosaurus araucanensis han mostrado que tanto los jóvenes como los adultos de esta especie habían desarrollado glándulas salinas.

facts.statement: Salt glands allowed Cricosaurus to drink seawater from birth and eat prey with the same ionic concentration as seawater, such as cephalopods, without dehydrating.
facts.quote: Esto significa que eran capaces de beber el agua de mar desde su nacimiento (un requisito para un animal de vida pelágica) y podía comer presas que tuvieran la misma concentración iónica que el agua marina circundante (por ejemplo, cefalópodos) sin tener que deshidratarse.

facts.statement: C. suevicus fed on fish, while Dakosaurus maximus was the top predator in its ecosystem.
facts.quote: C. suevicus se alimentaba de peces, mientras D. maximus era el depredador superior.

facts.statement: C. suevicus and Dakosaurus maximus lived contemporaneously in the Nusplingen Plattenkalk formation in southern Germany at the end of the Kimmeridgian stage.
facts.quote: De la algo más antigua formación Nusplingen Plattenkalk (a finales del Kimmeridgiense) del sur de Alemania, se sabe que las especies C. suevicus y Dakosaurus maximus eran contemporáneas.

facts.statement: Cricosaurus lived from the Oxfordian to the Valanginian stages, between 159 and 132.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Oxfordian to Valanginian (159 to 132.6 million years ago)

facts.quote: La cadera de Cricosaurus araucanensis posee varias características que crean una abertura pélvica inusualmente grande.

facts.statement: Herrera et al. considered viviparity more likely than oviparity for Cricosaurus and other metriorhynchids.
facts.quote: En una evaluación de las diferentes hipótesis reproductivas para Cricosaurus y otros metriorrínquidos, Herrera et al. consideraron que el viviparismo es más probable que el oviparismo.

facts.statement: Some phylogenetic analyses did not support the monophyly of Cricosaurus.
